items.title: Only Supreme Court can say its judgment will not be cited as precedent: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently held that only the Supreme Court can give a caveat that its judgment will not be cited as a precedent. A Division Bench of Justices C Hari Shankar and Vinod Kumar said that such a power is not available to any other court. “This caveat is, therefore, unique to the Supreme Court, as its decisions are constitutionally binding by virtue of Article 141 of the Constitution of India,” the Bench explained. It said that even if the facts of a case are similar to those in an earlier Supreme Court judgment, a lower court cannot treat that judgment as binding precedent if the Supreme Court itself has clarified that it should not apply in such circumstances. In such cases, the binding effect of Article 141 of the Constitution would not apply. Further, the Bench reasoned that if other courts say that their judgments will not be cited as a precedent, it could result in a situation in which similarly placed litigants would receive different treatment. “Ex facie, this would be impermissible,” the Court added. Justice C Hari Shankar and Justice Vinod Kumar The High Court rendered these observations as it upheld a Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) order. The CAT had granted a retired Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) scientist ante-dated in situ promotion under the Flexible Complementing Scheme (FCS). The Court ruled that his further promotion must still be assessed. Notably, the Central government had challenged the CAT order before the High Court, arguing that the recruitment rules and Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) memoranda bar retrospective promotion. It was also that the FCS is a merit-based scheme requiring screening, interview and committee assessment. However, the High Court rejected this argument. It held that the case was covered by a Supreme Court’s and its own ruling in Nakul Dev v Union of India. Pertinently, it was the Nakul Dev judgment of the High Court which carried a caveat that it could not be cited as precedent. The Central government had relied on this judgment. CGSC Balendu Shekhar with advocates Krishna Chaitanya and Divyansh Singh Dev appeared for Union of India. Advocates Sudarshan Rajan, Hitain Bajaj and Ria Setiya appeared for respondent Om Prakash. items.title: Persons enabling foreign nationals to get fake Aadhaar, PAN cards must be prosecuted: Bombay High Court
items.summary: The Bombay High Court has directed the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) to furnish before it within two weeks the documents submitted by an alleged foreign infiltrator in order to procure an Aadhaar card. [State of Maharashtra v. UIDAI & Ors] A Bench of Justices AS Gadkari and Kamal Khata issued the directive on a petition filed by the Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS), Navi Mumbai. Justice AS Gadkari and Justice Kamal Khata The case stems from a March 2018 raid in Juigaon, Panvel, where five Bangladeshi nationals were arrested after illegally entering India. Investigators revealed that the accused procured PAN cards, Election ID cards and Aadhaar cards using bogus documents with help from local facilitators. While UIDAI complied with a trial court order for other co-accused, records regarding respondent Bakaar Hasan Shaikh remained undisclosed, prompting the ATS to invoke Section 33(1) of the Aadhaar Act. The Bench allowed the petition and underlined the security threat posed by infiltration. “Foreign Nationals infiltrating Indian border have penetrated deep inside our country. By procuring Pan Card, Election ID Card and Aadhar Card from the concerned Authorities by submitting bogus documents, they present themselves as Indian citizens. This is a matter of serious concern and needs to be investigated by the concerned Investigating Agency expeditiously,” the judges said. The judges highlighted the urgency of prosecuting domestic accomplices. “The persons/co-accused who are helping such Foreign Nationals in infiltrating the Indian border and helping them in settling in our country by helping them further in procuring the Pan Card, Election ID Card and Aadhar Card must also be thoroughly interrogated and if their role is revealed in the said crime, they must be prosecuted for their illegal acts as per the provisions of law and the investigation must be taken to its logical conclusion,” the court recorded in its order. The observations follow similar orders passed on July 27 and August 10 where the Bench warned that fake Aadhaar cards create cascading vulnerabilities across identity, immigration, and security systems. In earlier cases involving Afghan and Bangladeshi infiltrators, the Court ordered joint inter-agency action, immediate deportations, document cancellations, and urged the Centre to amend the Aadhaar Act. Additional public prosecutor PP Shinde appeared for State. Advocate Supriya Kak appeared for UIDAI. [Read order]

items.title: Delhi SEM court orders release of Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka
items.summary: A Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court in Delhi on Wednesday ordered the release of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Ritu Raj , acting as the SEM, passed the release order after accepting the sureties furnished by Das and Ranka. Delhi Police had earlier sought an extension of judicial custody by three more days. The police had detained Das and Ranka on October 13 after they climbed the gates of the barricaded Jantar Mantar site On October 14, they were sent to judicial custody for five days. On October 19, the custody was extended for two more days. In its October 19 order, the SEM court said that Das and Ranka's conduct showed that they have no respect for the law and that there are serious concerns about them breaching peace and tranquillity. The Court said that they showed "habitualness" by calling for protest at de-notified areas. Further, the SEM rejected the sureties produced for Ranka and Das after finding them unfit. After the two-day period ended today, they were produced before the Court today. Meanwhile, Das and Ranka had also challenged the SEM court's October 19 order before the Delhi High Court. However, the writ petition was withdrawn after High Court Justice Subramonium Prasad said that the SEM Court was seized of the matter today and that a more appropriate remedy for them would be a revision plea if they do not get relief from SEM court. Advocates Abhik Chimni and Pranjal Abrol appeared for Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka before SEM court and High Court.

items.title: From consumer consent to competition control: The vires of Rule 5(6)
items.summary: The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026, notified on September 9, 2026 under Section 101(2)(zg) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, contain a provision that deserves closer scrutiny than its privacy-facing language suggests. Rule 5(6), which takes effect on January 1, 2027, provides that no marketplace e-commerce entity shall use information collected by it: - first, for the sale of goods, directly or indirectly, by any seller, whether related or not, bearing a brand or name common with that of the marketplace or - second, to promote or advertise any seller as being associated with the marketplace, unless express and affirmative consent for such use has been obtained from the consumer concerned. The provision speaks the language of consent, but the conduct it regulates has an obvious competition dimension as regards a marketplace using what it knows about consumers to advantage a connected seller over others on the same platform. The question this raises is not whether such conduct should be regulated, but whether the Consumer Protection Act authorises the Central government to regulate it through delegated legislation. Even the reach of the consent clause is contested. The words “unless … consent” sit within the second limb and some practitioners read the first limb as an outright prohibition that consent cannot unlock, while the government’s press release and other commentary describe the consent requirement more broadly. On the narrower reading, the first limb applies whatever the consumer wants and a restriction that no consumer choice can lift is hard to explain as a measure protecting consumer choice. The CCI’s unfinished investigation Closely related conduct is already before the Competition Commission of India (CCI). In January 2020, in Case No. 40/2019 , the CCI directed an investigation into Amazon and Flipkart on information concerning the online sale of smartphones, identifying four practices - the exclusive launch of mobile phones, preferred sellers, deep discounting and preferential listing or promotion of private labels. Its prima facie concern was framed under Section 3(1) read with Section 3(4) of the Competition Act, 2002. The probe has been in litigation for most of its life. A single judge of the Karnataka High Court dismissed the platforms’ writ petitions on June 11, 2021, a Division Bench dismissed their appeals on July 23, 2021 and on August 9, 2021, the Supreme Court declined to interfere. items.title: Bombay High Court fines junior advocate ₹25k, clerk ₹10k for unauthorised video recording of court proceedings
items.summary: The Bombay High Court recently fined a junior advocate and an advocate’s clerk after the clerk was caught illegally recording courtroom proceedings on his mobile phone [ Nagendra Kanojiya v. CEO, SRA & Ors ]. A Bench of Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale directed the junior advocate to pay ₹25,000 and the clerk to deposit ₹10,000 with the High Court Employees Medical Welfare Fund within two weeks. The Court also ordered the seizure of the mobile handset on which the video was recorded and the deletion of the recording. Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale The incident occurred during the hearing of a batch of petitions concerning a slum rehabilitation project. Prothonotary and Senior Master AH Laddhad (a senior administrative official) spotted the clerk recording the proceedings from the corridor and immediately alerted the Bench. The clerk stated he was filming under the instructions of a junior in the chambers of another advocate. The Court expressed disbelief over such conduct. “ We are really surprised. The advocates of this court are the first persons who are required to adhere to the rules of the court. We may state that there is an express bar to record court proceedings under the rules framed by the High Court,” the Court held. The Court added that this was a case where contempt of court proceedings could have been initiated, or where the Bar Council could have been directed to take action against the junior lawyer. However, it refrained from doing so after observing that the errant lawyer was a junior who appeared to lack basic training and etiquette to be followed as an advocate. Instead, the Court ordered both individuals to submit unconditional undertakings that they will not engage in similar misconduct in future. The Court warned that any recurrence of such acts will be viewed more sternly. "Any further violation of the prohibition against recording Court proceedings, shall be viewed with utmost seriousness and shall invite appropriate proceedings in accordance with law, including proceedings for contempt of Court," it said. The order comes days after the same Bench fined a government employee ₹10,000 and confiscated his mobile phone for secretly recording court proceedings with his camera flash turned on. At the time, the Bench also flagged the rising trend of unauthorised recordings being manipulated and circulated on social media. [Read order]

items.title: Employer can't use confidentiality clause to stop ex-employees from joining rival firms: Bengaluru Court
items.summary: A Bengaluru court has held that employers cannot prevent former employees from joining rival companies merely by invoking confidentiality agreements [EOX Vantage Private Limited Vs Shruti BS] Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge JV Kulkarni made the observation on October 6 while dismissing a suit filed by EOX Vantage Private Limited against its former employee, Shruthi BS, who was accused of leaking confidential information, poaching employees and soliciting clients. The Court said employers can legitimately protect trade secrets, proprietary information, confidential pricing, customer data and commercially valuable information. However, it clarified that restrictions preventing a person from carrying on a lawful profession, trade or business would be void under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act. " Therefore, an employer ordinarily cannot prevent a former employee from joining a competitor or using their general skills, experience and knowledge merely by calling the restrictive confidential clause," the Court said. EOX Vantage, a company providing back-office and knowledge process outsourcing services, approached the Court seeking a permanent injunction to restrain Shruthi from soliciting its employees, former employees and clients, and from disclosing confidential information. According to the company, Shruthi had access to sensitive business information while working as an Assistant Manager (Operations). It alleged that after leaving the company, she collaborated with other former employees to share confidential information with competitors and divert business. The company claimed that an internal investigation revealed unauthorised transfers of company data, including contracts and pricing information, to personal email accounts. It also alleged losses exceeding ₹20 lakh and referred to a criminal complaint registered against the former employees. Shruthi denied the allegations and maintained that she had resigned on medical grounds in April 2022. She argued that the company had accepted her resignation and issued a relieving letter after scrutinising her records. After examining the evidence, the Court found that the company's internal investigation report did not establish any specific wrongdoing by Shruthi. It noted that the employees, whose WhatsApp conversations and emails were relied upon, had not been examined. items.title: Tiger Shroff firing: Mumbai court remands three accused to police custody till October 31
items.summary: The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court at Esplanade in Mumbai on Wednesday remanded three accused in the Tiger Shroff firing case to the custody of the Mumbai Police Anti-Extortion Cell (AEC) until October 31. The accused have been identified as Rehan, Ritik Kurmi and Phool Singh. They were produced before the magistrate after being brought to Mumbai from Kota. The prosecution sought police custody to investigate the conspiracy behind the incident which occurred on the evening of October 18. Assailants fired five to six rounds at Shroff's car in Juhu. While he escaped relatively unhurt, his driver and a bystander sustained injuries. The Mumbai Police kater registered an FIR for attempt to murder and offences under the Arms Act. After the shooting, the accused allegedly abandoned their motorcycle in Andheri and attempted to flee to Nepal via Surat, Jaipur, and Delhi. They were intercepted by Kota police. Investigations suggest a link to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, which claimed responsibility for the attack in an unverified social media post. Police allege that Rehan was in contact with a foreign-based gang associate. Advocate Ajinkya Mirgal appeared for the accused in Mumbai. The Delhi Police Special Cell has also arrested four additional suspects for allegedly supplying the firearms used in the attack. Police claim a pistol and 20 rounds were procured from Amritsar on the foreign contact's instructions and transported to Mumbai by a female accused. Custodial interrogation is currently underway to ascertain the exact motive behind the shooting.

items.title: Lawyer can't be faulted for asking NCLT to upload its order on website: NCLAT
items.summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) recently held that an advocate cannot be faulted for sending an email to the court master of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) requesting that a judicial order passed by NCLT be uploaded on its website [Mrinal Vs Hynite] The order copy had remained unavailable for 18 days after the pronouncement. A bench of Judicial Member Justice Mohammad Faiz Alam Khan and Technical Member Naresh Salecha deleted the adverse remarks made by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) against advocate Mrinal Harsh Vardhan, who had emailed the NCLT court master asking that the order be uploaded. The NCLAT found that the email was polite and merely reflected the advocate's anxiety to obtain the order. " Naturally when the order which was pronounced in the open Court on 05.06.2026 could not be uploaded for 18 days, we do not find any error in the act of the Appellant in sending an e-mail to the Court Master of the concerned Bench, requesting only for the uplodation of the order which was admittedly pronounced in the open Court on 05.06.2026 ," the NCLAT observed. The case arose from insolvency proceedings concerning Hynite Farms Private Limited. On June 5, the NCLT pronounced an order concerning the approval of a resolution plan. However, the order was not uploaded for several days. Vardhan, who represented the Resolution Professional, subsequently emailed the Court Master requesting that the same be published on the NCLT website. The email explained that the order was urgently required to implement the approved resolution plan, particularly in view of Supreme Court directions requiring coordination with the NOIDA authority. However, the NCLT made adverse observations concerning the advocate's conduct in its orders dated June 5 and July 6. Aggrieved, Vardhan approached the NCLAT, arguing that the email was neither scandalous nor improper. He also submitted that the remarks could adversely affect his professional reputation and had been made without hearing him. The respondents did not oppose his request. After examining the email, the NCLAT agreed that the advocate had done nothing wrong. " We have also perused the e-mail which clearly shows that the language of the same is quite soft ," the NCLAT observed. It also noted that the order had not been uploaded for 18 days despite being pronounced in open court. Accordingly, the NCLAT expunged the adverse observations while clarifying that its decision could not be relied up

items.title: Telangana CM Revanth hikes ex gratia for families of police personnel killed on duty
items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy on Wednesday, October 21, announced an increase in ex-gratia payments for families of police personnel killed in the line of duty. Speaking at the Police Martyrs Memorial in Goshamahal, CM Revanth directed Director General of Police (DGP) CV Anand to increase the ex-gratia payment for the families of Home Guards from Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh. The ex-gratia amount for families of Superintendents of Police (SPs) and IPS officers was increased from Rs 1 crore to Rs 2 crore, while the ex-gratia amount for families of head constables and Additional SPs will be between Rs 1 crore and Rs 1.5 crore, compared with the Rs 45 lakh they received earlier. “The increase was not merely financial assistance but is a marker of respect for the families of the martyrs,” CM Revanth said. He also announced that all vacant posts in the state police department would be filled by 2028. Revanth also spoke of the induction of 112 Deputy Superintendents of Police (DSPs) as an unprecedented initiative in the history of the state, marking the single largest batch of direct-recruit DSPs to join the Telangana police. Speaking about TG SAFE, Revanth remarked that it was established to take a firm stance against food adulteration, while 'Spandana' – a set of 'Immediate Protection Teams' – was another initiative enforced to provide instant safeguarding for women and children during emergencies. items.title: Being apolitical in India is a luxury and an illusion  | LME 171 | Pooja Prasanna
items.summary: How many times have you heard someone say "I don’t get into politics. I just focus on my career" Or when there are protests, you hear people ask, "Why does everything have to be politicized?" It may sound balanced. But let us be honest for a second. In India, being "apolitical" is a luxury. It is also an illusion, and frankly, it is impossible. Every week on Let Me Explain , we break down complex things—a law, a court judgment, or a government policy. But today, I want to make a simple submission. Being apolitical is plain laziness, and complaining about "politicizing" an issue, any issue, is complete hogwash. Let me explain. Sitting on the fence is not neutrality. It is a decision, a choice. You are deciding to back the status quo. Politics is not restricted to Parliament or election rallies. Politics is the price of your groceries. It is the quality of the air in your lungs, the speed of your Wi-Fi, the fairness of your exams, and whether you get home safely at night. When you say, "I’m not interested in politics," you are actually saying, "The system works fine enough for me, so I don't need to care." That is just privilege. It is the privilege, of caste and class, of not being worried that those who are drunk on power will not come for you. It is the privilege of living in a decent or good house with private water tankers, diesel power backups. It is not caring how bad the education system in the country is because you can just send your kids abroad. It is the luxury of not being hit by price raise and food inflation. Or the rate of unemployment. Comedian Vir Das put it quite well recently: saying you are apolitical is not an ideology. It is just comfort. Detachment is a luxury for the well-fed. Before I go ahead, a quick pause. This is festival season and many of you are celebrating the triumph of good over evil, here’s something worth thinking about. Who gets to decide what is good, what is evil, and who gets to define the battle? Those are political questions too. So this festive season, don’t just celebrate- instead ask questions about the world we live in, the people who govern us, and the choices that shape our lives. items.title: Chennai rains: T Nagar, Velachery and other areas face waterlogging
items.summary: Heavy intermittent rainfall since Tuesday night, October 20, has caused waterlogging in several Chennai neighbourhoods, including T Nagar, Velachery, Nungambakkam, Ashok Nagar, and West Mambalam. The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has deployed motor pumps, tractors, and other machinery to remove stagnant rainwater. Civic workers have also been working on clearing blockages in drains and directing the water into the stormwater drain network. In T Nagar, rainwater accumulated on several major roads, including Panagal Park Road and Habibullah Road, as well as streets adjoining Thirumalai Road. Panagal Park Road, an important stretch connecting Anna Salai to T Nagar, was severely waterlogged. Two-wheelers, buses, autorickshaws, and cars struggled to navigate the road, with water reaching halfway up some vehicles. Traffic along this stretch has also been affected by ongoing Metro Rail construction on one side and stormwater drain works on the other. Bazullah Road and streets adjoining Thirumalai Road were also affected. Waterlogging was reported on GN Chetty Road too, where infrastructure works had been undertaken under the Smart City project. Water resources Minister and T Nagar MLA Anand said precautionary measures have been put in place under Chief Minister Vijay's instructions and that preparations had been underway for a month. “Previously, rainwater would remain stagnant for two or three days. Now, we are using motor pumps to remove the accumulated water within three to four hours,” he told the media. The Minister also said the government was planning to distribute breakfast to 2,000 people on Wednesday morning and had made arrangements to serve approximately 5,000 people at lunchtime. Heavy rainfall has been reported across several parts of Tamil Nadu since the onset of the Northeast Monsoon. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast the possibility of heavy rainfall in the state for the next two days. In Velachery, heavy overnight rain inundated AGS Colony, where approximately 25 houses were affected. Minister for Information Technology and Velachery MLA Kumar visited the locality and heard residents' grievances. items.title: Supreme Court temporarily stays probe in CMRL–Exalogic case; FIRs remain
items.summary: The Supreme Court (SC) on Wednesday, October 21, temporarily stayed the investigation into the Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL)–Exalogic case involving alleged payments to former Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter Veena T, and his son-in-law, former minister Muhammed Riyaz. The SC also set aside the Kerala High Court’s order refusing to hear an appeal against the direction to register a First Information Report (FIR). Following the High Court’s direction, the Kerala Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) registered FIRs and began investigating Pinarayi Vijayan, Veena and Riyaz. The SC stayed the investigation for a week but clarified that the FIRs would remain in place for now. According to LiveLaw , the SC said Pinarayi and his family could appeal to a High Court division bench against the single judge’s direction to register an FIR. Pinarayi Vijayan and his family approached the SC on October 16, a day after facing a setback in the Kerala High Court over the FIR registration in the CMRL–Exalogic case. The High Court single judge had directed the registration of an FIR based on a report submitted by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to the Kerala police. Earlier, the VACB had registered two FIRs following the High Court’s direction. Pinarayi is named as the first accused in one case, while Riyaz is the first accused in the other. Veena is named as the second accused in both. The FIRs allege corruption and conspiracy in connection with payments made by CMRL and an associated company to Veena and her now-defunct firm, Exalogic. On October 13, Pinarayi, Veena and Riyaz filed separate appeals challenging a single judge’s order directing the VACB to register an FIR under the Prevention of Corruption Act. The order concerned alleged financial dealings between CMRL and Exalogic Solutions Pvt Ltd; but the High Court dismissed their appeals, refusing to interfere with the direction to register an FIR. The division bench, comprising Justices K. Natarajan and Johnson John, held that an accused person in a corruption case has no legal right to be heard before an FIR is registered.
